turns.zh: 至少对于货币，我们是这样称呼的。你摄入大量信息，实际上 LLM 可能能更好地处理它。所以，10 年前我做这个的时候，我们没有这些工具。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: But now I see that. And then then I moved to the buy side where you start paying for alternative data exactly like like you like you did. We were actually one of the very first few at Balyasny to do the X firehose or Twitter firehose. That's something like a stupidly expensive like $300,000 a month like data thing that you have to pay for to get all tweets. Um and and you sort of priced it. It used to I don't think I don't know if it was ever free. It was free for researchers.
turns.zh: 但现在我看到了。然后我转到买方，你开始为另类数据付费，就像你一样。我们实际上是 Balyasny 最早做 X firehose 或 Twitter firehose 的少数人之一。那是一种愚蠢地昂贵的东西，比如每月 30 万美元的数据，你必须付费才能获取所有推文。嗯，你有点给它定价。它曾经我不认为我不知道它是否曾经免费。它对研究人员免费。

turns.en: But then if you're like a hedge fund, you have to sort of buy that. And it's very noisy. So then my eyes go up because I don't know if I would trade on those things because sometimes people do just talk random crap and sometimes people try to manipulate markets by saying stuff and it just doesn't matter that much. But we would also have alternative asset data like satellite information or credit card information and whatever, right? And so, on the buy side, my number one question is: are you looking at my data? Which is probably not. But how would you assure people? How do you integrate with systems that you don't necessarily even see?
turns.zh: 但如果你是对冲基金，你就得买那些数据。而且噪音很大。所以我会警惕，因为我不确定我会不会根据那些东西交易，因为有时候人们就是胡说八道，有时候人们试图通过放话来操纵市场，而那并不那么重要。但我们也会有另类资产数据，比如卫星信息或信用卡信息等等，对吧？所以，在买方，我的头号问题是：你在看我的数据吗？大概没有。但你怎么让人放心？你如何与那些你甚至不一定看到的系统集成？

turns.en: Yeah, and I think that's two questions in there. The first one is: if there's so much data available, how do you know what's important? So when we're looking at X data, it's a natural conversation when we speak to people—or let's even expand it out to any types of data. One thing we found with people is they really will have their trusted people who they'll follow, these voices in industry. Especially in commodities, they'll be the suppliers of commodities, they'll be the LNG, all of these facilities who will be active on that because it's the quickest way for them to also give a status update.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为这里面有两个问题。第一个是：如果可用的数据这么多，你怎么知道什么重要？所以当我们看 X 的数据时，我们与人交谈时自然会有对话——或者让我们扩展到任何类型的数据。我们发现人们确实会有他们信任的人，他们会关注这些行业声音。尤其是在大宗商品领域，他们会是商品供应商、LNG 设施等，这些设施会活跃在上面，因为这是他们提供状态更新的最快方式。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: So it's interesting because we found that a lot of our users will tell us about this. So it's like, "Oh, okay. So you find it as a trusted source because you believe this certain individual."
turns.zh: 所以很有趣，因为我们发现很多用户会告诉我们这一点。所以就像，“哦，好的。所以你认为它是一个可信来源，因为你相信某个特定个人。”

turns.en: Sketchy.
turns.zh: 有点可疑。

turns.en: Right? And so it's one of those things where we have found a way to try and filter out as much as possible, but when we are showing it to someone, we give a confidence score. Of, okay, someone is saying this one thing, but this is everything else happening around the conversation. Because what's interesting to people is if there are divergent sources. Like, an example would be how many ships are going up, how many planes are going above us right now. If Reuters is saying something or Bloomberg is saying something and Wall Street Journal is saying something, they may not all agree. But the fact that they don't agree is a point of data because is there an opportunity there because no one knows. So that's how we try and give people information. And then the second question is, you know, people's data sits everywhere. And I think there's different types of integration. The first one is what about their messy PDF data? That data is what we've built a vision language model to understand. So we'll take the data that they can upload to their cloud version of Moshi. And then we actually go and break it down and then build it up in our database. And there are certain types of data where you just have to connect to their systems. And then that's more of a conversation.
turns.zh: 对吧？所以这是我们找到的一种方法，尽量过滤掉噪音，但当我们向某人展示时，我们会给出一个置信度分数。比如，某人在说这件事，但这是对话周围发生的所有其他事情。因为对人们来说有趣的是，如果有不同的来源。比如，一个例子是现在有多少艘船在航行，有多少架飞机在我们上方飞过。如果路透社在说某事，彭博社在说某事，华尔街日报在说某事，他们可能并不都同意。但他们不同意的事实本身就是一个数据点，因为那里是否有机会，因为没人知道。所以这就是我们试图向人们提供信息的方式。然后第二个问题是，人们的数据无处不在。我认为有不同类型的集成。第一种是他们的杂乱 PDF 数据怎么办？我们已经构建了一个视觉语言模型来理解这些数据。所以我们会获取他们可以上传到 Moshi 云版本的数据。然后我们实际上会去分解它，然后在我们的数据库中构建起来。还有某些类型的数据，你只需要连接到他们的系统。然后那更多是对话。

turns.en: Is it important to—I assume you're running this vision language model yourself. Is it important to own that or would you want to offload it? I mean there's any number of vendors. Reducto is like a known document processing one. How important is it to have your own models versus just use whatever's off the shelf?
turns.zh: 重要的是——我假设你们自己运行这个视觉语言模型。拥有它重要吗，还是你想外包？我的意思是，有很多供应商。Reducto 是一个知名的文档处理公司。拥有自己的模型有多重要，而不是直接用现成的？

turns.en: I think that's the question that a lot of companies are battling with right now. The first question for us is: if someone's giving us their data, we don't want to be sending it to a third party because there are systems out there which can do these things for you. But you may want to make sure that you've got that agreement on how are they processing that data? What are they doing with it? That's the first question. The second one is: if you don't have a team of engineers, then that is a great solution. But if you do have a team of engineers like us—a fun fact is most of the team has in some capacity worked with NASA—then they want to build the models.
turns.zh: 我认为这是很多公司现在正在纠结的问题。对我们来说，第一个问题是：如果有人给我们他们的数据，我们不想把它发送给第三方，因为外面有系统可以为你做这些事情。但你可能想确保你有协议，关于他们如何处理数据？他们用数据做什么？这是第一个问题。第二个是：如果你没有工程师团队，那么那是一个很好的解决方案。但如果你有像我们这样的工程师团队——一个有趣的事实是，团队中大多数人都在某种程度上与 NASA 合作过——那么他们想要构建模型。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: But not everyone has that. And so, you know, I think it really depends on where you are as a team.
turns.zh: 但不是每个人都有。所以，你知道，我认为这真的取决于你作为一个团队所处的位置。

turns.en: Yeah, got it. Um, okay, and then coming into your talk, you apparently had a lot of inbound from it. Which I'm—this is our first finance focused one. So I was genuinely unsure
turns.zh: 是的，明白了。嗯，好的，然后说到你的演讲，你显然从中获得了很多关注。这是我——这是我们的第一个金融 focused 活动。所以我真的不确定

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: could get in the door. Obviously we like pitched it and marketed very heavily for this crew. What kind of people did you end up talking to?
turns.zh: 能不能进门。显然我们为这群人做了很多推销和营销。你最终和什么样的人交谈？

turns.en: Yeah. We—it was a fantastic opportunity because we have been back-to-back speaking to people. And what we initially thought would be the interest, we've had people like in the past hour message me on LinkedIn saying, "Hey, I saw your core talk. Are you in Houston? Can we get a meeting?" Or, "Hey, are you in New York? Can we get a meeting?" The types of people we've had: a lot of traders, either at funds, consulting. And then AI engineers was an interesting one because a lot of them are feeling overwhelmed with the pressure from management.
turns.zh: 是的。我们——这是一个绝佳的机会，因为我们一直在连续与人交谈。我们最初以为的兴趣点，过去一小时有人在 LinkedIn 上给我发消息说：“嘿，我看了你的核心演讲。你在休斯顿吗？我们能见个面吗？”或者，“嘿，你在纽约吗？我们能见个面吗？”我们遇到的人的类型：很多交易员，要么在基金，要么在咨询。然后 AI 工程师是一个有趣的群体，因为他们中的很多人对管理层的压力感到不堪重负。

turns.en: To do what?
turns.zh: 做什么？

turns.en: Because people now say we don't need a team, you are the team. And so it's like, "Hey, I need to now build this whole system myself, but that system would typically be done by 10 people." So a lot of people have talked to us and they're like, "Hey, I need to build a system, but like, you know, do I need to have a swarm of agents? But then like, what if something breaks?" Something interesting is, "Hey, I built the system. People told me they needed it. It's in the email. No one's clicking it, but they complain that they have this problem. Like, what do I do?" So that was that one area. And then partnerships. You know, we've been meeting people and people like, "Hey, you're doing this? That's interesting because we're doing this. Let's have a conversation after." So I've actually extended my stay in New York because we've—now I was meant to leave today. We've now got meetings on Thursday, extended another day Friday, extended it another day Monday. And then I've got now meetings where people are like, "Hey, we're in energy. Let's talk in Houston." So we've filled up a week after the conference of meetings.
turns.zh: 因为现在人们说我们不需要团队，你就是团队。所以就像，“嘿，我现在需要自己构建整个系统，但那个系统通常需要 10 个人来完成。”所以很多人和我们交谈，他们说：“嘿，我需要构建一个系统，但是，你知道，我需要一群智能体吗？但然后，如果出问题了怎么办？”有趣的是，“嘿，我构建了系统。人们告诉我他们需要它。它在邮件里。没人点击它，但他们抱怨他们有这个问题。我该怎么办？”所以那是其中一个领域。然后是合作伙伴关系。你知道，我们一直在见人，人们说：“嘿，你在做这个？那很有趣，因为我们在做这个。我们之后聊聊。”所以我实际上延长了在纽约的停留，因为我们现在——我本来今天要走。我们现在周四有会议，延长一天到周五，再延长一天到周一。然后我现在有会议，人们说：“嘿，我们在能源领域。我们在休斯顿谈。”所以我们会议排满了会议后的一周。

turns.en: Oh my god.
turns.zh: 天哪。

turns.en: Yeah. And my team was like, "Hey, Annica, another person signed up. Another person signed up." So it's super cool.
turns.zh: 是的。我的团队说：“嘿，Annica，又有人报名了。又有人报名了。”所以超级酷。

turns.en: Is it interesting to do these one-to-one? I guess because they need to ask you things in private. It just seems very inefficient to set up so many meetings when you could be doing building a business or building a product.
turns.zh: 做这些一对一的会议有趣吗？我猜是因为他们需要私下问你事情。当你本可以建立业务或构建产品时，安排这么多会议似乎非常低效。

turns.en: Yeah, we try and be as helpful to people where we will have an initial meeting, but then really we want to be able to understand what the problem is that you're solving for and then have a plan after that.
turns.zh: 是的，我们尽量对人有帮助，我们会有一个初步会议，但然后我们真的想能够理解你要解决的问题是什么，然后之后有一个计划。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So we have things that we're doing now to stream that, because we're hosting our first webinar because of the amount of inbound that we have. We just can't always do these one-to-ones.
turns.zh: 所以我们现在有一些办法来分流这些需求，因为我们正在办第一场网络研讨会，因为收到的咨询太多了。我们没法总是做这种一对一的会面。

turns.en: And more generally, when I was on the buy side, the banks would actually set up these meetings for us. And they'd come to little rooms like this. There'd be sort of a round table. I would meet five at once. So I'd say I'm a CFO of a company and I need to do investor relations. I'm meeting five funds at once. I know, be one of the five funds.
turns.zh: 更一般地说，我在买方的时候，银行其实会帮我们安排这些会面。他们会来到像这样的小房间。有点像圆桌。我一次见五个人。比如我说我是一家公司的 CFO，我需要做投资者关系。我一次见五家基金。我知道，你就是那五家基金之一。

turns.en: And I imagine what we could do for you in future — which I haven't got this off the ground yet, but we should do the meetings on site. Like you've —
turns.zh: 我在想我们未来能为你做什么——这个我还没落地，但我们应该把会面放在现场做。就像你——

turns.en: That makes sense.
turns.zh: 这说得通。

turns.en: People saw your talk, they want to speak more with you. They should be able to sign up and you can do five-on-one. And probably all these questions are the exact same. And like —
turns.zh: 大家看了你的演讲，想多跟你聊聊。他们应该能报名，然后你可以做五对一。而且这些问题大概都一模一样。就像——

turns.en: That would be a great idea, actually. Because another —
turns.zh: 那其实会是个很棒的主意。因为另一个——

turns.en: 'Cause we used to do this in finance, like —
turns.zh: 因为我们以前在金融行业就这么做，就像——

turns.en: That is such a good idea, 'cause we had one where sometimes you don't know what the person you're meeting looks like as well.
turns.zh: 那真是个好主意，因为我们有过这种情况，有时候你都不知道你要见的人长什么样。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: So you're trying to take pictures of where you are to say like, hey, meet me here, meet me here, and like call them. So an idea like that would be great.
turns.zh: 所以你会拍下你所在位置的照片，说，嘿，来这里见我，来这里见我，然后给他们打电话。所以这样的点子会很棒。

turns.en: Room, yeah.
turns.zh: 房间，对。

turns.en: It's like, hey, like —
turns.zh: 就像，嘿，就像——

turns.en: I mean, this whole floor is there, but we had to pre-assign it to other speakers, but we wanted to do some dynamic allocation. I just don't know how to get that going. I think I'm trying to feel it out with you.
turns.zh: 我是说，整层楼都在那儿，但我们得把它预先分配给其他演讲者，不过我们想做些动态分配。我只是不知道怎么推动起来。我想我是在跟你试探一下。

turns.en: So you're not having to fly to Houston, or even if they're in New York, you don't even have to go to their office. Everyone gets in here, gets the meetings done. You're out.
turns.zh: 这样你就不用飞到休斯顿，或者即使他们在纽约，你也不用去他们的办公室。大家到这里来，把会面做完。你就走了。

turns.en: I actually think that would be a great idea. Like have a 30-minute slot for this person and then like sign up or something like that.
turns.zh: 我其实觉得那会是个很棒的主意。比如给这个人留一个 30 分钟的时段，然后报名之类的。

turns.en: Whatever you want, right?
turns.zh: 随你定，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah, like smaller one-on-one. That is a great idea.
turns.zh: 对，像更小规模的一对一。那是个很棒的主意。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah. I mean, anything else that we could do better, or other experiences from the conference that you're —
turns.zh: 对，对。我是说，还有别的我们能做得更好的地方吗，或者你在这次大会上的其他体验——

turns.en: I think this has been the best organized conference I've been to.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是我参加过组织得最好的大会。

turns.en: Aw, you're just saying that.
turns.zh: 哎呀，你就是这么说说。

turns.en: Seriously. Like, the amount of good quality guidelines I've had, and it was super clear.
turns.zh: 说真的。比如我拿到的那些高质量指引，而且非常清楚。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Like, the speaker team, the breakout rooms, the speaker lounge, having — I feel like I've —
turns.zh: 比如演讲者团队、分组讨论室、演讲者休息室，有——我感觉我——

turns.en: The lounge is never this good. I will have to say that. Yeah, yeah. So, yeah. Haircut, I don't know, did you — what did you —
turns.zh: 休息室从来没这么好过。这点我得说。对，对。所以，对。理发，我不知道，你——你做了什么——

turns.en: No, I didn't do a haircut.
turns.zh: 没有，我没理发。

turns.en: Facial?
turns.zh: 做脸？

turns.en: I did a facial and a massage.
turns.zh: 我做了个脸和按摩。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: I know you got your haircut.
turns.zh: 我知道你理了发。

turns.en: Get my haircut. Yeah.
turns.zh: 理了发。对。

turns.en: I mean, we do want to spoil our speakers. This was definitely the over and above, and that's thanks to Cognition for doing that. But, yeah, organizing is one thing. I do think in terms of business value and efficiency, I think that's an important element. Like, we want to make this something that's useful for you for both hiring and selling, you know? And I don't know how to balance that because —
turns.zh: 我是说，我们确实想宠一宠我们的演讲者。这次绝对是超规格了，这要感谢 Cognition 这么做。但，对，组织是一回事。我确实认为在商业价值和效率方面，那是个重要元素。比如，我们想让这个活动对你在招聘和销售两方面都有用，你知道吗？我不知道怎么平衡这个，因为——

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: What's more important to you, hiring or selling?
turns.zh: 对你来说哪个更重要，招聘还是销售？

turns.en: So in terms of — we've just hired, and we plan to hire. We're always meeting people, but the priority right now is to meet clients.
turns.zh: 就——我们刚招了人，也计划招人。我们一直在见人，但现在的优先事项是见客户。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: That's the priority, not necessarily hiring, because I think what we have with hiring is we get continuous inbound from LinkedIn.
turns.zh: 那是优先事项，不一定是招聘，因为我觉得在招聘方面，我们一直能从 LinkedIn 收到源源不断的咨询。

turns.en: Really?
turns.zh: 真的吗？

turns.en: Yeah. We had one job up. We had to close it. It was open for 4 days. We had 2,500 applicants.
turns.zh: 对。我们挂了一个职位。我们不得不把它关了。它开放了 4 天。我们收到了 2500 份申请。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: And so it's like that's tough to deal with in itself, but meeting people who want to buy, and people who — because I think there's people who have the problem but they don't want to buy. And there's people who have the problem and want to buy, and you're trying to find that match. That is — I haven't found any person who's done that.
turns.zh: 所以光是应付这个就很难了，但见那些想买的人，还有那些——因为我觉得有些人有这个问题但不想买。还有些人有这个问题又想买，而你要试着找到那个匹配。那是——我还没找到任何做到这一点的人。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Well, but so, I really like your one-on-one idea.
turns.zh: 不过，我真的很喜欢你这个一对一的主意。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah. I mean, so basically, I'm transferring over what I used to have as a hedge fund person to this market, which is AI in finance.
turns.zh: 对，对。我是说，基本上，我把我以前做对冲基金时的那套东西搬到这个市场，也就是金融领域的 AI。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: We'll try to do that next year. We'll try to be the definitive thing. And I think on the hiring side — so that's buying, and then that's clear. I think I can definitely help you better there. On the hiring side I also want to help you, right? Like 2,500 is too much and most of it is noise. And so you need a better filter.
turns.zh: 我们明年会试着这么做。我们会试着做成那个标杆。我觉得在招聘方面——那是买方，那很清楚。我觉得我在那方面肯定能更好地帮你。在招聘方面我也想帮你，对吧？比如 2500 太多了，大部分都是噪音。所以你需要一个更好的筛选器。

turns.en: I have a strong opinion.
turns.zh: 我有个强烈的看法。

turns.en: Okay, go ahead.
turns.zh: 好，请讲。

turns.en: The amount of people who are also doing it in a way where it's like undercover, not — it's —
turns.zh: 还有很多人是以一种类似卧底的方式在做，不是——是——

turns.en: They're shopping, they're spying?
turns.zh: 他们是在摸底，是在刺探？

turns.en: You have that, but you also have — they're legally not allowed to work. So there's so much noise in that.
turns.zh: 有那种情况，但也有——他们在法律上不被允许工作。所以那里面噪音很多。

turns.en: Visas?
turns.zh: 签证？

turns.en: Visas, and there's so much noise around that as well. And so when I was a first-time — like I am a first-time founder — well, when I first started, you don't know those things. You don't know the market, right? And there's a lot of noise related to that.
turns.zh: 签证，那方面也有很多噪音。所以当我第一次——比如我是第一次创业的创始人——嗯，我刚起步的时候，你不懂那些东西。你不了解市场，对吧？而且有很多相关的噪音。

turns.en: Yeah, okay. Well, we'll try to get that higher signal for you. We want to be a high signal conference. I'm just appreciative that you're spending some time with us and congrats on your success.
turns.zh: 对，好。我们会试着为你提供更高信号。我们想做一个高信号的大会。我很感激你花时间跟我们聊，也恭喜你取得成功。

ts.sec: How the host moved into AI

turns.en: Thank you so much. I'd love — I have one question, which is how you — when you moved into AI?
turns.zh: 非常感谢。我很想——我有个问题，就是你怎么——你是什么时候转入 AI 的？

turns.en: Just decided to start. Well, I left the HFT world and moved into tech. And then when the AI wave happened, I realized that I better move very, very quickly to establish this field. And so I did the AI engineering post and started this conference and the media stuff, 'cause I'm very much of a media person.
turns.zh: 就是决定开始。嗯，我离开了高频交易的世界，转入科技行业。然后当 AI 浪潮来的时候，我意识到我最好非常非常快地行动，来建立这个领域。所以我做了 AI 工程方面的岗位，然后创办了这个大会和媒体那块，因为我很大程度上是个媒体人。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: At my heart. I do miss trading a little bit, but this is very fulfilling 'cause I get to meet real people instead of stare at a screen all day.
turns.zh: 骨子里是。我确实有点想念交易，但这很有成就感，因为我能见到真实的人，而不是整天盯着屏幕。

turns.en: Yeah, I feel the same.
turns.zh: 对，我也有同感。

turns.en: Well, thank you. I think we have to go.
turns.zh: 好，谢谢。我想我们得走了。

turns.en: Thank you so much. Thanks.
turns.zh: 非常感谢。谢谢。

turns.en: Thanks.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

consensus.en: AI should push relevant data to users proactively, not wait for queries.
consensus.zh: AI 应主动向用户推送相关数据，而非等待查询。

consensus.en: Recommendation systems are underappreciated but crucial for AI product adoption.
consensus.zh: 推荐系统被低估，但对 AI 产品落地至关重要。

consensus.en: Owning document-processing models matters when handling sensitive user data.
consensus.zh: 处理敏感用户数据时，自研文档处理模型很重要。

consensus.en: Divergent sources are themselves valuable data points for traders.
consensus.zh: 信源分歧本身就是对交易员有价值的数据点。

consensus.en: AI engineers face unrealistic pressure to build whole systems alone.
consensus.zh: AI 工程师面临独自构建整个系统的不现实压力。

consensus.en: Solving UI and recommendation together is key to software people actually use.
consensus.zh: 同时解决 UI 与推荐问题，是软件被真正使用的关键。

contrarian.en: Moshi is not a new Bloomberg; it's a different category of software.
contrarian.zh: Moshi 不是新彭博，而是另一类软件。

contrarian.en: Social media data is noisy and manipulable; confidence scores matter more than volume.
contrarian.zh: 社交媒体数据嘈杂且可被操纵，置信度比数据量更重要。

contrarian.en: Hiring inbound is overwhelming; client meetings are the real priority now.
contrarian.zh: 求职者涌入已过载，当前真正的优先事项是见客户。

contrarian.en: One-on-one meetings are inefficient; group sessions with five funds work better.
contrarian.zh: 一对一会议效率低，五个基金一组的会谈更有效。

contrarian.en: Building your own models beats off-the-shelf only if you have strong engineers.
contrarian.zh: 只有拥有强大工程师团队时，自研模型才优于现成方案。

contrarian.en: Most applicants are noise due to visa and undercover issues; better filters are needed.
contrarian.zh: 多数申请者是噪音，涉及签证和隐蔽求职问题，需要更好的筛选。
